The list of metric partition tags.

For metrics with queue

Default value:

Tag key: queue_name. Value: root.

When you use metrics with a queue, you can set the queue_name tag to specify the queue. Ensure that you enter the full queue hierarchy name.

Example

Metric name: yarn_resourcemanager_queue_AvailableVCoresPercentage

Tag:
`queue_name: root.default.a`

For metrics with partition

Default value:
Tag key: none. Value: none.
For metrics with a partition, you must set the partition_name tag and explicitly specify the partition name.

Example

Metric name: yarn_cluster_availMemoryMBByPartition

Tag: `partition_name: DEFAULT_PARTITION`

If RecurrenceType is set to DAILY, you can specify only one value. Valid values: 1 to 31.
If RecurrenceType is set to WEEKLY, you can specify multiple values separated by commas (,). MON, TUE, WED, THU, FRI, SAT, and SUN represent Monday through Sunday. For example, MON,FRI,SUN represents Monday, Friday, and Sunday.

fields.help_en: The type of private pool that you want to use to start ECS instances. A private pool is generated when an elasticity assurance or a capacity reservation takes effect. You can select a private pool for starting ECS instances. Valid values: Open, Target, and None. If you set the parameter to Open, the system selects an open private pool to start instances. If no matching open private pools exist, the resources in the public pool are used. In this case, you do not need to specify the ID of the private pool. If you set the parameter to Target, the resources in the specified private pool are used to start ECS instances. If the specified private pool does not exist, ECS instances cannot be started. You must specify the ID of the private pool when you set the parameter to Target. If you set the parameter to None, the resources in private pools are not used to start instances. Default value: None
